label: rem:gram-matrix-spectral-connection
title: Gram matrix of Markov pairing $\leftrightarrow$ Frobenius co-Casimir / $E_\infty$ pairing
html:
Remark (where the Gram matrix fits in the spectral-sequence / Frobenius framework).

Read every G^{-1} below on H_n/\mathrm{rad} \cong \mathrm{TL}_n, not on H_n. Corrected 2026-08-09. This remark was written under the excised convention C, where the antisymmetric weight y_{(1^3)} = 0.0227449\ldots is small but nonzero and G genuinely inverts. Under the production convention D the pin z(q^2+1) = q^3 forces y_{(1^3)} = 0 exactly, so the (1^3) block is the radical of the trace form and \det G = 0. Not "numerically singular" — zero. A G^{-1} computed under C is therefore not an approximation to one under D; the D one does not exist.

This remark already contains its own refutation. The Wedderburn paragraph below derives G_{\lambda\mu} = \delta_{\lambda\mu}\,\tau(e_\lambda) — block diagonal with the weights themselves on the diagonal. So \det G = \prod_\lambda \tau(e_\lambda)^{\,\cdot}, and convention D sends one factor to zero. The very next line then writes down G^{-1}_{\lambda\mu} = \delta_{\lambda\mu}\,[n]_q!/(\dim_q(\lambda)\dim(\lambda)), which for that block is a division by zero.

Nothing structural is lost, only relocated. The radical is a two-sided ideal (TemperleyLiebTower.traceRadical_two_sided), so \mathrm{tr}_M descends and the induced pairing on the quotient is non-degenerate. Ranks: \mathrm{corank}\,G = 1 at n = 3, 10 = 3^2 + 1^2 at n = 4, 78 = 6^2+5^2+4^2+1^2 at n = 5; what survives is \sum \dim^2 = C_n — the Catalan numbers 5, 14, 42.

Proved in MarkovGramDegenerate.lean: block_mem_radical → gram_det_eq_zero_of_radical_combination for the vanishing, pairing_descends and mem_radical_of_pairing_zero for the descent. Sorry-free.

Role of the Gram matrix. The Gram matrix G of the Markov pairing is the common algebraic object that encodes:

  1. The Frobenius algebra structure of the quotient H_n(R, q)/\mathrm{rad}\,\mathrm{tr}_M \cong \mathrm{TL}_n: the pairing \langle x, y \rangle_\tau := \tau(x \cdot y) is non-degenerate iff \det G \neq 0 (Frobenius Gram matrix). Under convention D that holds on the quotient and fails on H_n itself, where \det G = 0 exactly — see the correction above.
  2. The inverse G^{-1} — which exists on that quotient, not on H_n (convention D) — enters the Frobenius co-Casimir (Frobenius universal): C_{\dim_q} = \sum_{i, j} (G^{-1})_{ij} \cdot b_i \cdot b_j in a non-central-idempotent basis (standard Frobenius identity), with i, j running over the two-row stratum only.
  3. The spectral-sequence pairing: each E_\infty^{p, *} is paired with \mathrm{tr}_M via the Gram matrix restricted to the stratum — so E_\infty^{p, *}(T_w) \to R is really T_w \mapsto G_{T_w, *} projected to the stratum.
  4. The knot-factor Frobenius pairing (knot factor Frobenius pairing) computes G_{\beta, \beta^*} for braid-mirror pairs — the chirality factor a_K of Term 5 is a normalised Gram-matrix entry.

Gram matrix in the three derived terms.

term Gram matrix role
Term 1 (descended) G_{T_w, \mathbf{1}} = \tau(T_w) — single matrix entry
Term 2, 3 (brane tower) G_{\sigma_i, \sigma_i} = \tau(\sigma_i^2) = hz + 1; pair G_{\sigma_i \sigma_j, \sigma_j \sigma_i}
Term 4 (Frobenius co-Casimir) \tau(C_{\dim_q}) = \mathrm{tr}(G^{-1} \cdot D) where D_{ij} = \delta_{ij}/\dim_q per block basis — on the non-degenerate quotient H_n/\mathrm{rad} \cong \mathrm{TL}_n (convention D; G is singular on H_n)
Term 5 (chirality) a_K = G_{\beta, \beta^*} / G_{\mathbf{1}, \mathbf{1}}
Term 6 (jet-prefix) G restricted to higher filtration strata

Gram matrix for H_3(R, q) over R.

Basis: \{1, \sigma_0, \sigma_1, \sigma_0 \sigma_1, \sigma_1 \sigma_0, \sigma_0 \sigma_1 \sigma_0\}. Markov trace on standard basis (Markov trace factorization): \tau(T_w) = z^{\ell(w)} for w \in S_n reduced, where \ell(w) is the length. So \tau(1) = 1, \tau(\sigma_i) = z, \tau(\sigma_i \sigma_j) = z^2. The naïve length rule z^{\ell(w)} fails for adjacent triples (the rule assumes the rightmost generator lies in the proper sub-algebra; this fails for \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 since \sigma_1\sigma_0 \notin H_2). The canonical Ocneanu--Wenzl recursion gives \tau(\sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0) = hz^2 + z (formerly stated as z^3; since corrected).

Gram matrix G_{ij} = \tau(b_i b_j^{-1}) (cyclic self-pairing). The first-row/column entries shown as z^3 below are uncorrected: by the recursion just quoted they should read hz^2 + z:

  G \;=\;
  \begin{pmatrix}
    1 & z & z & z^2 & z^2 & z^3 \\
    z & 1 + hz & * & * & * & * \\
    z & * & 1 + hz & * & * & * \\
    z^2 & * & * & * & * & * \\
    z^2 & * & * & * & * & * \\
    z^3 & * & * & * & * & *
  \end{pmatrix},

with off-diagonal entries computed via Hecke relations.

At q = q_0, \det G \neq 0 (generically), confirming the Frobenius property. Retracted 2026-08-09 — this is the convention-C reading. Under the production convention D, \det G = 0 at q = q_0 and at every generic q: the vanishing is forced by the pin z(q^2+1) = q^3, not by a coincidence at a special point, so "generically" does not rescue it. H_3 is not a Frobenius algebra under \mathrm{tr}_M; the 5-dimensional quotient H_3/\mathrm{rad} \cong \mathrm{TL}_3 is.

Gram \leftrightarrow Wedderburn conjugation. In the central-idempotent basis \{e_\lambda\}, the Gram matrix is block-diagonal: G_{\lambda, \mu} = \delta_{\lambda \mu} \cdot \tau(e_\lambda^2) = \delta_{\lambda \mu} \cdot \tau(e_\lambda) = \delta_{\lambda \mu} \cdot \frac{\dim_q(\lambda) \cdot \dim(\lambda)}{[n]_q!}. The inverse — on the surviving blocks only, since under convention D the radical blocks have \tau(e_\lambda) = 0 — is G^{-1}_{\lambda, \mu} = \delta_{\lambda \mu} \cdot \frac{[n]_q!}{\dim_q(\lambda) \cdot \dim(\lambda)}. Summing G^{-1} diagonal times 1/\dim_q gives exactly the Frobenius co-Casimir trace \sum_\lambda 1/\dim_q(\lambda) — recovering (Frobenius universal).

The inversion in the previous sentence is only valid block-by-block on the surviving blocks. The block-diagonal form G_{\lambda\mu} = \delta_{\lambda\mu}\tau(e_\lambda) is correct under either convention and is the sharpest statement in this remark: it shows \det G is a product of the Wedderburn weights, so G inverts iff every weight is nonzero. Under the excised convention C that held. Under convention D it does not — y_\lambda = 0 for every \lambda with \ell(\lambda) \geq 3, since the fibre is the two-dimensional fundamental of \mathrm{SU}_q(2) and no three-row partition survives Schur–Weyl. For those \lambda the displayed G^{-1}_{\lambda\lambda} divides by zero, and the co-Casimir sum \sum_\lambda 1/\dim_q(\lambda) must run over the two-row stratum only. Restricted there, every statement above stands unchanged — which is precisely the sense in which the Frobenius structure survives on \mathrm{TL}_n.

The quantum dimensions \dim_q(\lambda) entering this Wedderburn block structure are the Wedderburn-block face of the q-Laplacian spectral tower (the q-Laplacian spectral tower): at a root of unity q = e^{i\pi/\kappa} they truncate to the finite Verlinde/ADE set, so the Gram matrix becomes finite block-diagonal modular-tensor data there.

Gram-matrix rank and the spectral sequence.

The filtration J^\bullet(q) induces a block structure on G: entries G_{ij} with b_i \in J^p and b_j \in J^{q} sit in the (p, q)-block. The filtered Gram matrix has block-triangular shape in the standard basis (since \tau(J^p \cdot J^q) \subset J^{p+q} generically), and its diagonal blocks G^{(p)} := G|_{J^p/J^{p+1}} are the pairings on E_0^{p, *}. The spectral-sequence differentials d_r are encoded in the off-diagonal blocks of G under filtered inversion.

So the Gram matrix is the single algebraic object whose block structure generates the entire spectral sequence and its mass-term identification. Computing G explicitly for H_3(R, q) (spectral-sequence H3 explicit) is equivalent to computing all pages E_r^{p, *}.
